narrative.overview:
Bird-Watcher is one survey notebook carried into every kind of work. The app is the book: a cover-yellow spine runs the full height of the left edge, each workspace is a thumb-indexed section pulled out of it, and every task is a numbered entry: written onto survey-green ruled ledgers on a cool white waterproof page, and on the board carried as a separate page tile in a lane washed with the board's own ink. The page is dense by design. Rows sit at 40px, columns are captioned in pre-printed condensed caps, and numerals are measured in a tabular mono, so a full screen of entries reads as a ledger rather than a feed.

State is printed, never decorated. Done is a strike drawn across the entry key, progress is a half-filled square, story points are a dot that grows on a fixed magnitude ramp, and overdue changes the ink to chestnut without changing the geometry of the row. The ruling continues to the foot of every page body, so empty space is blank lines waiting for entries rather than grey canvas. At night the page turns bottle green and the spine stays yellow, dimmed against glare.

The world refuses the category default for task trackers: floating rounded cards on a grey canvas, pill badges, and an avatar-heavy sidebar. The board's tiles (a user-directed change for at-a-glance distinction) are not that card: they are page-coloured slips with 2px corners and a 1px rule border, lying flat on a tinted lane with no shadow.
keyCharacteristics: A full-height cover-yellow spine with thumb tabs; the active tab is page-coloured and flush with the page.
Survey-green ruling at one pixel, with a 3px double rule under every page header and column caption row.
Barlow Condensed caps for everything pre-printed; Barlow for written entries; Overpass Mono for keys, dates and tallies.
Corners of 0 to 2px on anything that holds text. Circles exist only as magnitude dots and chart point markers.
Board lanes are washed with the board's ink; entries on them are page tiles held by a 1px rule-mid border, never a shadow.
Anything that takes focus over the page (entry drawer, command palette, shortcut sheet) dims the rest with a scrim, holds a 2px ink edge, and closes on an outside click.
Chestnut is the only attention ink.
Day page and night page are equal citizens, switched by system preference or an explicit choice.

rules.name: The Single Warning Ink Rule
rules.body: Chestnut is the only colour that means "attend to this". Overdue, blocking, error and destructive actions use it; nothing else does, and no second alarm colour (red, orange) is ever introduced.

rules.name: The Cover Is Material Rule
rules.body: Yellow belongs to the cover: the spine, the auth cover, and the primary button that is pressed into it. It never becomes a page background, a highlight band on rows, or a badge fill.

rules.name: The Ink Changes, Geometry Doesn't Rule
rules.body: Overdue and urgent states change ink colour and weight; they never change row height, add borders, or add badges.

rules.name: The Shape Tells The Ink Rule
rules.body: Epics and labels share six inks; the mark's shape carries the meaning. A vertical 3px tick is always an epic (16px tall in a margin, 12px inside a tile's epic tag); a square swatch is always a label. Never give a label a tick or an epic a swatch.

rules.name: The Lane Wash Rule
rules.body: A board's colour reaches the board only as a wash on its lanes: the ink mixed into ground in oklab at the lane-tint strength (10% by day, 4% by night). It never colours text, tile fills, tile borders, the spine or the header.

rules.name: The Series Ink Is Not Text Rule
rules.body: Chart series inks fill lines, bars, point markers, legend keys and swatches only. Axis values, data labels and readouts are set in ink or pencil.

rules.name: The Printed Versus Written Rule
rules.body: Anything that would be pre-printed on a field book form (captions, titles, tabs, buttons) is Barlow Condensed uppercase. Anything a person writes (entry titles, epic titles, sprint names, label names, descriptions) is Barlow in sentence case. Never set user content in stamped caps.

rules.name: The Measured Numeral Rule
rules.body: Every number that is data (keys, dates, tallies, points) is Overpass Mono with tabular figures and a slashed zero.

rules.name: The Title Stands Alone Rule
rules.body: A page header carries no caption, kicker or label above or before its title. Context comes from a linked breadcrumb (workspace / ) on the same baseline.

rules.name: The Ruled To The Foot Rule
rules.body: No page body ends on blank canvas. Ruling continues below the last entry to the bottom of the page at the 40px row pitch (My Work, Inbox, Activity, Table, Backlog). Board lanes are the user-directed exception: they hold tiles on tinted ground and are not ruled.

rules.name: The Paper Has No Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces separate by rule lines, tone (page versus page-sunk versus cover) and overlap, never by drop shadows or blur.

rules.name: The Modal Page Rule
rules.body: Anything that takes focus over the page is another page, not a floating panel: the scrim dims what is behind it (160ms fade in), a 2px ink edge or frame holds it, and a click on the scrim closes it. No shadow, no blur, no rounded corners.

rules.name: The Lifted Slip Rule
rules.body: Anything picked up is a slip of paper: a -1deg tilt and a 1px ink border. Lift is never a shadow or a scale-up.

rules.name: The No Pills Rule
rules.body: No capsule shapes: no pill badges, pill buttons, pill tabs or pill toggles. Radius never exceeds 2px on anything that holds text.

dos: Do keep the cover-yellow spine full height on desktop and as a top band on phones; it is the book.
Do close every page header, ledger caption row, drawer header and palette input with the 3px double rule in rule-strong.
Do rule every page body to its foot at the 40px row pitch; board lanes end in tinted ground instead.
Do put board entries on page tiles with a 1px rule-mid border, 2px corners and 8px gaps, on lanes washed with the board's ink.
Do dim the page with the scrim behind the entry drawer, command palette and shortcut sheet, hold them with a 2px ink edge or frame, and close them on an outside click.
Do express state as printed marks: struck keys, status squares, magnitude dots, ink changes.
Do set every data number in Overpass Mono with tabular figures and slashed zero.
Do design every surface for both the day page and the night page.

Do use the shared motion curve cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1): 120ms for state, 160ms for the tab pull, the drop and the scrim fade, 200ms for the drawer slide, 260ms for the strike; collapse to near-zero under reduced motion.
Do separate epics from labels by shape: the 3x16 tick for an epic, the 8px swatch or printed tag for a label.
Do give every chart with two or more series a legend and a "Show as table" view.
Do draw checkboxes with the drawn checkbox, never the browser's own.
donts: Don't use floating rounded cards on a grey canvas, pill badges, or an avatar-heavy sidebar; a board tile lies flat with 2px corners and a rule border.
Don't round anything that holds text beyond 2px; circles are reserved for magnitude dots.
Don't add drop shadows or blur for depth.
Don't introduce a second attention colour beside chestnut.
Don't draw an epic's ink as a full-height coloured edge stripe on rows or panels; it is a 3x16px tick in the margin.
Don't set text in a chart series ink or an epic/label ink.
Don't lift a dragged item with a shadow, or separate the drawer, palette or shortcut sheet from the page with a shadow or blur; the scrim and the 2px ink edge do that work.
Don't let the board colour reach text, tile fills, tile borders or the spine; it is a lane wash only.
Don't put a caption, kicker or eyebrow label above or before a page title.
Don't set user-written content in stamped uppercase.
